sense: fix a day or time for something

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation: diem + dative of the event
terms.comment: The day goes in the accusative and the event in the dative: diem conloquiō cōnstituere, to schedule a meeting. Agreed with someone: cum aliquō cōnstituere (Cic. Verr. 2.2.65, Lewis & Short). As scheduled: ut erat cōnstitūtum (Cic. Clu. 37, Lewis & Short); on the scheduled day, diē cōnstitūtā (Caes. BG 1.4.2). The noun schedule, a timetable, is hōrārium (see schedule).

phrases.latin: utī aut iterum conloquiō diem cōnstitueret aut, sī id minus vellet, ex suīs lēgātīs aliquem ad sē mitteret
phrases.english: (he asked) that Caesar should either fix a day for another meeting or, if he did not want that, send him one of his officers

phrases.latin: Diē cōnstitūtā causae dictiōnis Orgetorīx ad jūdicium omnem suam familiam, ad hominum mīlia decem, undique coēgit
phrases.english: On the day fixed for his trial Orgetorix gathered his whole household at the court, some ten thousand men, from all sides

sources: Caesar, BG 1.4.2 and 1.47.1, checked against the Perseus Latin texts.
